sections.title: Vertically Integrated Power Strategy
sections.body: Energy is the single largest operational cost for any data center, accounting for up to 70% of OPEX. Kenya AI Compute circumvents high public utility rates through a captive generation model. By integrating our modular data center with a dedicated power plant, we capture the 'energy arbitrage' opportunity. We generate electricity at an industrial cost of $0.04-$0.06/kWh, whereas the standard grid rates for data centers in most countries range from $0.15 to $0.25/kWh. Our hybrid generation mix primarily uses natural gas and solar, with diesel generators providing N+1 redundancy. This ensures that even in the unlikely event of a primary generation failure, our AI workloads continue to run without interruption. This strategy not only protects our margins but also offers our clients long-term price stability that is impossible to find in traditional cloud markets. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models.
